newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Labour ready for possible by-election - Clark.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Labour ready for possible by-election - Clark.

text.p: Labour leader Helen Clark said on Friday that her party would be "more than happy" to fight a by-election in the electorate of disgraced New Zealand First MP, Tukuroirangi Morgan.
"I think it is very sad, so soon after an election, that this issue arises but I think we would be in a strong position," Clark said on Radio New Zealand.
Political commentators said that if it came to a by-election in Morgan's Te Tai Hauauru seat, Labour was likely to win.

Morgan admitted on Thursday he sought payment for a television interview after first denying the claims, embarassing his party leader and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters. Peters had previously backed Morgan's initial denial.
Clark said the reason Morgan had survived a string of embarrassments was his relationship with NZ First deputy leader, Tau Henare, who is also his brother-in-law.
"The problem is there is just incredible, overwhelming arrogance. He cannot accept that he does anything wrong," Clark told Radio New Zealand.
Asked why Peters had retained Morgan after ejecting Michael Laws last year for misleading conduct, Clark said it was because Peters feared the reaction of his deputy, Tau Henare.
"If you go back to the Mr Laws affair, Mr Morgan has done exactly what Mr Laws did -- misled Mr Peters, caused Mr Peters to make a fool of himself.
"In that case Mr Henare was very against Mr Laws continuing in parliament. He was the one who put the pressure on Mr Peters to get Mr Laws to go.

"In this case Mr Henare is the brother-in-law. He is very linked emotionally to Mr Morgan, and I'm sure that were Mr Peters to push Mr Morgan aside, that could be the trigger for Mr Henare, Mr Morgan and possibly two of the other NZ First MPs going to form their own party," she said.
"That is the reality we are facing," she said.
